nodes.title: rc5 fixes: defects found while preparing rc5

acceptance: group-nodes --into-new NEW_ID accepts a NEW_ID held by one of the listed nodes or a descendant of one: the free-id check ignores the listed nodes' subtrees, as move-node --id ignores the moved subtree. A NEW_ID held by any node outside those subtrees, malformed, or not a direct child id of the common parent is refused with today's message, exit 1, nothing written

tests/test_outline_group_cli.py: siblings M1.1, M1.2 (with child M1.2.1 and a registry claim on M1.2) and M1.3 grouped --into-new M1.2 give M1.1 -> M1.2.1, M1.2 -> M1.2.2, M1.2.1 -> M1.2.2.1 and M1.3 -> M1.2.3; the printed map omits the new parent; every renamed sheet holds its own node's text, the claim's node_id is M1.2.2, the graph validates once, and the same run with --rewrite-refs rewrites prose through that map. A refused case leaves the tree byte-for-byte unchanged

POST /api/outline/group reaches this through group_nodes with unchanged request and response shapes; tests/test_gui_outline_contract.py gains one case for this input and its existing cases and the PM GUI Python API tests (tests/test_gui_app*.py, tests/test_roadmap_gui_*.py) pass unchanged

group-nodes --into-new help and the group-nodes rule in docs/roadmap-authoring.md say NEW_ID may be an id one of the listed nodes holds; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Fixed entry. Out of scope: move-node, indent and outdent, apply (M21.5), a GUI control
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about +25, tests about +50, docs about +3
nodes.title: group-nodes accepts a new parent id held by one of the nodes it groups

acceptance: In the transaction that renames a planning sheet (move-node, indent, outdent, group-nodes, the PM GUI move, indent, outdent, group, and reorder with renumber_outline: true), a touch zone equal to that sheet's old path is rewritten to its new path, in the project-relative form (planning/<sheet>) and in the checkout-relative form (<project root>/planning/<sheet>, e.g. sr/planning/...) alike, on the nodes and registry claims the move already rewrites (the move's scope); no other zone changes

validate prints one warning (stdout or stderr as the existing zone warnings do; exit code unchanged, also under --strict) for each zone on a live node of any status that names a .md file directly under the planning dir, in either form, that does not exist in the working tree, naming the node, the zone and, when the zone's trailing _<node_key>.md matches a node, that node's current planning_dir. Staged or unstaged makes no difference. A zone naming an existing sheet, or any other missing path, keeps today's handling

Tests: a move of a node whose zones name its own sheet in both forms (and a claim with the same zones) rewrites all of them and validates silently; a hand-made stale sheet zone gets the warning before and after git add; a Not Started node with a missing non-sheet zone keeps today's notice. The GUI outline contract test and the PM GUI Python API tests pass unchanged (shapes unchanged; the GUI paths share stage_id_rewrite)

docs/roadmap-authoring.md (move-node rewrite list and the touch_zones row) states both; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Fixed entry. Out of scope: rewriting zones on nodes outside the move's scope (the warning reports them), prose (M21.3), decisions (M22.3)
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about +45, tests about +60, docs about +4
nodes.title: A move rewrites touch zones that name a renamed planning sheet, and validate warns on a zone naming a missing sheet

acceptance: Every id-changing move (move-node, indent, outdent, group-nodes, --renumber-outline and the PM GUI move, indent, outdent, group, and reorder with renumber_outline: true) rewrites, in the tracked roadmap/decisions.yaml, the node field of every entry (any kind and status) whose node equals an old id in the move's old -> new map, in the same AtomicWritePlan as the chunk, sheet and registry rewrites, always (not only with --rewrite-refs); each id is looked up once, so chains and swaps stay correct; a refused move leaves the ledger byte-for-byte unchanged; the file is written only when an entry changed

validate prints one stdout notice (exit code unchanged, also under --strict) listing each open decision or human-action entry and each active preference in the tracked ledger whose node names no live node; closed entries are not checked (they may name archived or removed nodes); no ledger, or an unreadable one, adds nothing beyond today's output

Tests: a move with the ledger holding an open entry, a closed entry and a preference on moved ids, plus one on an unmoved id, rewrites exactly the moved ones; a swap via --renumber-outline; a refused move; the notice for an open entry on a missing id and silence for a closed one. The GUI outline contract test and the PM GUI Python API tests pass unchanged

docs/roadmap-authoring.md (move-node rewrite list) and docs/orchestration.md (ledger section) state that moves rewrite node and what validate checks; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Fixed entry. Out of scope: decisions.local.yaml, storing node_key in the ledger, schema changes, rewriting ids inside summary or answer text
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): package about +40, tests about +60, docs about +4
nodes.title: Moves rewrite decision-ledger node ids, and validate warns on an open entry naming no node

acceptance: The feature and gate sheet templates' References line 'Roadmap chunk for `{{NODE_ID}}`' no longer contains the display id (for example 'Roadmap chunk: the node this sheet's file name names'); a sheet scaffolded by add-node, scaffold-planning, group-nodes or the PM GUI add contains no display id anywhere in its body, and the template's own rule (do not repeat id or node_key in the body) holds

Tests: group-nodes --into-new M1.9 then move-node M1.9 --id M1.4 leaves a group sheet whose text names neither M1.9 nor M1.4; scaffold-planning for a task and for a gate produces a body without the node id; tests/test_planning_sheet_bootstrap.py and the existing template tests pass with only the changed line's assertion updated

planning_sheet_bootstrap keeps its public functions and signatures (render_planning_sheet_template still takes node_id); CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Fixed entry. Out of scope: rewriting existing sheets (they keep their line; --rewrite-refs or rename-refs fix them), the planning README, any validator
Estimated net line change (informational, not a gate): templates about 0, package about -2, tests about +20
nodes.title: New planning sheets no longer write the node's display id into their body
